correctness.rationale: The Schur-Horn majorization inequalities are converted by the Ky Fan principle to all rank-k projection supports. Projecting a rank-k projection to the traceless tangent space gives squared Frobenius norm k(d-k)/d, so the exact distance from any candidate center to each support orbit is explicit. Requiring all such distances to be at least r yields the complete center inequalities. Orthogonal averaging proves the scalar center attains the global maximum, giving the inradius and contact ranks. For the circumradius, all orbit extreme points have common centered Frobenius norm, convexity contains the whole orbitope in that sphere, symmetry forces the unique minimum-enclosing-ball center to be scalar, and strict convexity identifies the outer contact set. Repeated eigenvalues and all k from 1 through d-1 are included.

value.rationale: Schur-Horn orbitopes are a canonical and widely studied family of spectral convex bodies. The finding computes both basic Euclidean radii for every spectrum, gives the complete incenter locus, and identifies the exact rank orbits responsible for inball contact. For the standard orbitope it yields simple closed forms in every dimension. These are natural intrinsic metric invariants tied directly to the majorization geometry, not an arbitrary finite slice, parameter renaming, or recomputation of a known table.
